topics.topic: Outcome precedence when cleanup is unconfirmed alongside timeout, resource exhaustion, a recorded trap, or another outcome condition
questions: When cleanup is unconfirmed and the wall deadline or a resource limit was also hit, does cleanup force `crashed(cleanup_failed)`, or does rule 5's first matching outcome remain `timeout` or `resource_exhausted`?
When a trap was recorded and cleanup is later unconfirmed, does the execution become `sandbox_violation` as rule 4 says for any recorded hit, or `crashed(cleanup_failed)` as A03-3 and A03-5 say?

When cleanup is unconfirmed together with a timeout, resource limit, recorded trap, abnormal exit or contract violation, does cleanup override the rule 5 order and force `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`, or does the first rule 5 outcome remain?

If a function output exceeds both `output_bytes` and `stored_value_bytes_max` and cleanup is also unconfirmed, does A15 still require `resource_exhausted`, or does A03-4 require `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`?

When `cleanup_unconfirmed` coincides with an earlier condition in this unqualified first-match order, must cleanup override it as A03 rules 7, A03-4 and A03-5 require, or must the first condition here decide?
Does a recorded trap still require `sandbox_violation` when cleanup is unconfirmed, or is `cleanup_unconfirmed` a third exception that requires `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`?

quotes:
Outcomes are closed and checked in this order, the first that holds
   deciding: wall deadline passed — `timeout`; a limit hit (memory, process count,
   scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`; a trap of rule 4 raised —
   `sandbox_violation`; the module failed to load, has no `run`, raised, or the
   process exited abnormally — `crashed`; the returned dict does not have exactly
   the output ports, or a value fails its port's schema, or a file output is not
   `bytes` — `contract_violation`; otherwise the execution succeeded.

A03-4: outcome = crashed(cleanup_failed)  IF cleanup_unconfirmed
                 ELSE first_of(timeout, resource_exhausted, sandbox_violation, crashed,
                               contract_violation, succeeded)
judgement.divergence: One implementation preserves the first ordinary outcome such as `timeout`, `resource_exhausted` or `sandbox_violation`; another overrides it with `crashed(cleanup_failed)` when cleanup is unconfirmed, which the caller and trace readers observe.
judgement.why: The unqualified closed first-match order says its first applicable condition decides, while A03-4 makes unconfirmed cleanup override that entire order.

witness.initial: An existing implementation can be tried, and its sandbox execution can pass the wall deadline before cleanup is attempted.
events: The function busy-loops until the wall deadline passes.
The parent terminates the environment but cannot confirm that cleanup completed.
witness.observer: The requesting agent and later readers of the TrialExecution.
basis:
Trying an implementation (State 0 action), by any agent,
   executes an existing implementation on the cases of its contract version's
   corpus that the request names, all of them when it names none, in corpus
   order, records one TrialExecution per case and returns them.

An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped
   and the exchange directory is removed. If that cannot be confirmed the output
   is discarded, the execution is recorded `crashed` with detail
   `cleanup_failed`, and the kernel process stops; runs it left `running` are
   recovered on the next start (A14 rule 5).

basis:
Trying an implementation (State 0 action), by any agent,
   executes an existing implementation on the cases of its contract version's
   corpus that the request names, all of them when it names none, in corpus
   order, records one TrialExecution per case and returns them.

Each trap, before raising, writes its hit to the
   runner's channel to the parent, which user code cannot unsend; any recorded hit makes the
   execution `sandbox_violation` under the order of rule 5, even when the code
   catches it and returns a conforming output: `timeout` and `resource_exhausted`
   still come first.

An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped
   and the exchange directory is removed. If that cannot be confirmed the output
   is discarded, the execution is recorded `crashed` with detail
   `cleanup_failed`, and the kernel process stops; runs it left `running` are
   recovered on the next start (A14 rule 5).

topics.topic: Expected success outcome name in the A03-4 test
questions: Must this A03-4 test assert the execution outcome `succeeded`, which A03-4 names, or the TrialExecution outcome `passed`, which M07 names after case evaluation?

quotes:
A case passes when the execution succeeded and, if the case states expected
   outputs, every output's digest equals the expected one — a file output is
   recorded in the TrialExecution by digest, size and media type, keeps no bytes,
   and is compared with the expected file fixture by digest; a `many` file output
   equals its expected list when both have the same length and the digests are
   equal position by position, so order and repetitions count; outputs that
   validate but differ are `output_mismatch`.
judgement.why: The sandbox execution succeeds, and case evaluation maps that success to the TrialExecution outcome `passed`; the Required test uses the latter layer's name.

precedent.topic: Number and reuse of wall-clock and monotonic readings within an operation
quotes:
Every timestamp the kernel records comes from one clock module; no other part
   of the kernel reads the wall clock. A request never supplies the current time.

Deadlines of one sandbox execution and one HTTP request are measured with the
   monotonic clock of the same module; a monotonic reading is never stored.
precedent.why: These clock-reading rules are unchanged from the closed text, and the transition did not alter when readings are taken or reused.
